question: Do spring strength and retained velocity each provide a distinct useful control over a reproducible target-driven motion?
hypothesis: With identical target disturbance, changing spring strength changes response timing and changing retained velocity changes persistence/overshoot; both must be demonstrated rather than labelled organic drift.

parameter.name: spring strength and velocity retention investigated separately
parameter.unit: per explicit logical update; no seconds conversion

baseline.kind: planned source-extracted investigation harness, not historical survey baseline
baseline.policy: Explicit authored values; no public default or recommended range claim.

comparison.input: Nine fixed sites: x=[96,256,416], y=[128,320,512], row-major. Each target receives(+100,0) at tick0; initial velocity zero; source return-to-spawn0.04 applies before every spring update; mouse=(10000,10000). Every candidate uses the same complete sequence.
comparison.drawing: Ordinary marks at current positions and recorded trajectories; fixed colours/styles across all variants, no font/assets/shader.
metrics: displacement and velocity at every required tick
maximum displacement and any sign reversal of velocity
per-frame changed-pixel fraction and MAE against the authored baseline
direct inspection of every distinct required frame
comparison.claim: Diagnostic motion response only; no full source web or historical pixel comparison.

constraints: At most7attempted render processes total: one baseline and six variants; failures consume the budget.
One coefficient changes per variant; all initial state, target inputs, return policy and styles identical.
Register source/harness hashes and exact outputs before first render.
Use original MIT-noticed Point body in a temporary-copy investigation or an independently specified equivalent diagnostic; name any substitution explicitly.
Do not modify survey or upstream source.
Root serializes renders and preserves all attempts under .work.
No automatic continuous range inference; zero and retention1 are diagnostic boundary cases, not promised useful settings.
decision_rules: Retain each coefficient only if its controlled change yields a distinct explainable temporal effect in both recorded state and inspected frames.
If a control is masked or its effect requires changing the other coefficient, reconsider exposure or define an explicitly coupled model rather than inventing an independent range.
Do not label an undamped/nonsettling response invalid solely because it does not return within the observation window; distinguish intentional oscillation from arithmetic failure.
Reject autonomous drift as the described capability; equilibrium must remain still.
Leave recommended defaults and continuous encouraged ranges absent unless this investigation provides sufficient evidence.
prerequisites: Root review of diagnostic implementation and the exact target/event sequence before rendering.
Separate retained-state/step contract investigation; no public operation implementation authorized by this experiment alone.
